clue.text: Language that's gone beyond reductio ad absurdum

indicators.note: the solver must go past the first words of the Latin phrase and look inside its last word for the letters

explanation.surface: A tongue has been taken so far that it ends in logical absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone beyond reductio ad' sends you past those words into 'absurdum', where abs-URDU-m holds the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a national tongue of Pakistan, closely related to Hindi.

clue.text: Head demanding stripper, look, in uniform

indicators.note: one piece is set inside the other, as the clue places look in uniform

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means alike, all the same
lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: A stripper demands that someone look at her, in uniform, as head of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible story Salome danced (the dance of the seven veils, hence 'stripper') and asked for the head of John the Baptist.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical dancer asked Herod for John the Baptist's head as her reward.

clue.text: When lifting present about to cry a tiny, tiny bit

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the present moment is now
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Someone raising a gift is close to tears over a very small piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the cry inside the present, and 'lifting' turns that whole run upward, as a down entry reads. 'a tiny, tiny bit' is a subatomic particle, not a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The W particle is a subatomic carrier of the weak force, an extremely small piece of matter.

clue.text: Status lacking, group value having enough members

parts.note: the phrase status quo with the word status taken away leaves only quo
a rate is a price or value

explanation.surface: A committee's standing is poor until it has the numbers it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take 'status quo', remove 'status' and QUO is left; 'group' belongs to the surface, the quorum being a group's minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is quorate when enough people attend for its decisions to be valid.

clue.text: GP halts, recalling rash advice

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, means the letters of the phrase are read in reverse order

parts.note: a rash is a crop of spots, so advice about it is a spots tip

explanation.surface: A doctor stops working and reconsiders hasty guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: GP here is Grand Prix, not a family doctor: pit stops halt a racing car. Advice on a rash is a 'spots tip', which 'recalling' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a car pauses in the pits for fuel or tyres during a Grand Prix.

clue.text: Singer taken badly, not at home in Scotland

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of taken are put in a disordered arrangement

parts.note: awa is the Scots word for away, meaning out or not at home

explanation.surface: A performer fell ill while away north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns TAKEN into TEKAN; AWA is Scottish dialect for 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiri Te Kanawa is a celebrated New Zealand operatic soprano.

clue.text: Boy drinking a lot of beer — girl gets Evian water

indicators.note: drinking means the boy takes the other piece inside him

parts.note: Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard
a keg is a barrel, a large quantity of beer
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lad downs a barrel of beer while his girlfriend sticks to bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' places the barrel inside the boy. Evian is not the bottled water but the French town on the lake's shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian-les-Bains is a spa town on the southern shore of this Alpine lake.

clue.text: A number, distraught, mourn Marmite ban

indicators.note: distraught, deeply upset, signals that the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Fans are upset and grieve because a yeast spread has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges MOURN MARMITE BAN into the Bob Dylan song title. Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dylan song is a well-known piece of music, and a song is a number.

clue.text: Missing orders not on form

parts.note: lacking something, having run short of it
sorts are classes or orders of things

explanation.surface: Someone without instructions is performing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly unwell or irritable means being below one's usual condition.

clue.text: Guinness: 11 cold bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: the answer to 11 across followed by the word cold, read as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A stout drinker bottles a cold beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out the answer to 11 and add 'cold': internation-ALE C-old holds the actor's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Guinness was the English actor of Star Wars and The Bridge on the River Kwai.

clue.text: Test E number, but not the right one

definitions.text: number, but not the right one

parts.note: a test match is an international sporting fixture

explanation.surface: A trial of a food additive that turns out to be the wrong code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' means song, and 'not the right one' says it is a left-wing anthem rather than a correct E number.
explanation.definitionFit: The socialist anthem is a song of the political left, so not a song of the right.

clue.text: Silly being stern after new pay cut

indicators.note: after places the word for stern behind the other pieces
cut means the final letter of the word for pay is chopped off

parts.note: income is pay or earnings
the poop is the raised stern deck of a ship

explanation.surface: A foolish person grows severe after a fresh salary reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of the pay word; 'after' sets the ship's stern behind. 'stern' looks like an adjective meaning severe but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a fool, someone who acts in a silly way.

clue.text: Cheer the sad-are their hearts lifted?

indicators.note: lifted, in a down clue, means the letters are read upward
their hearts means the middle letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A question of whether gloomy people have had their spirits raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearts of 'the', 'sad' and 'are' are H, A, R; 'lifted' turns HAR upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of encouragement, short for hurrah.

clue.text: Pieces not quite long enough for Scheherazade?

definitions.meaning: chessmen that move in an L shape

definitions.text: not quite long enough for Scheherazade?
definitions.meaning: K stands for a thousand, so these are a thousand evenings, one short of the thousand and one of the Arabian tales

explanation.surface: Fragments that fall just short of the storyteller's needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Scheherazade told stories for 1001 nights; K for 1000 with NIGHTS is one too few.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: chess pieces, and a thousand nights, one short of the Arabian Nights tally.

clue.text: Gallons of this brewed quietly here for the present?

indicators.note: brewed means the letters are mixed up like ingredients

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A large quantity of this ale has been made at present, without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges OF THIS into IFTSHO. 'the present' is a gift, not now.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling souvenirs is where one buys a gift.

clue.text: City linked transport initially moving in two different directions

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word transport
moving signals that the letters of in two are rearranged

parts.note: W and N are the compass points west and north

explanation.surface: Urban transport runs both ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns IN TWO into WINTO; W and N are two compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A town paired with a foreign counterpart for cultural exchange is formally linked to it.

clue.text: Quietly Miliband, defending GB, expressed contempt

indicators.note: defenders play at the back, so the politician's name comes behind the writer's

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
GBS, George Bernard Shaw, is the playwright meant by GB here, giving his surname
Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken Labour politician protects Britain and scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: GB looks like Great Britain, but it is George Bernard Shaw. Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of disdain, so saying it shows scorn.

clue.text: Greetings for the husband

definitions.meaning: belonging to him, the male partner

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the greeting hi, and the masculine possessive pronoun.

clue.text: Tip for Hendry: use they designed rest

indicators.note: designed means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to a snooker champion to use the rest when stretching for a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges USE THEY. Stephen Hendry was a snooker champion, and a rest is the snooker cue support; 'Tip for Hendry' is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is sleep, a period of repose.

clue.text: Charles I's grave robbers might have made this Queen's order

definitions.text: Charles I's grave robbers might have made this
definitions.meaning: the king was beheaded, so thieves at his tomb might cry out about taking his head
the Queen of Hearts' constant command in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Body snatchers at a royal tomb echo a monarch's command.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I was beheaded in 1649; the Queen in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland orders beheadings constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand for beheading, both from the Queen of Hearts and plausibly from thieves stealing the king's skull.

clue.text: One exercises with college athletic club that encourages throwing events

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A student exercises with a university sports club that promotes javelin and discus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing events' sounds like athletics but means vomiting: ipecac is an emetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a root extract used medically to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Wells outside, abnormally large and fashionable for washing

indicators.note: outside means the writer's initials go round the other pieces

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the science-fiction author, gives his initials
OS is outsize, a clothing size for very large
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Big trendy wells are used for cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' is the author H. G. Wells, not water sources; OS (outsize) is a British clothing label for large sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spraying with a hose is a way of cleaning down.

clue.text: Work that teetotaller will back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a teetotaller will sup nothing, sup O, with O as zero

explanation.surface: A job that a non-drinker will support.
explanation.walkthrough: A teetotaller will 'sup O', drink nothing; read backwards it gives the musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition or artistic piece.

clue.text: Milliners lead off, dressed in unlikely fabric

indicators.note: dressed in means the trimmed word is clothed inside the other piece

parts.note: tall as in a tall story, one hard to believe

indicators.note: lead off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: hatters make and sell hats, as milliners do

explanation.surface: Hatmakers, minus their boss, are wearing an improbable cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead off' drops the first letter of the hatmakers; 'dressed in' wraps the result in the improbable word, tall as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattersall is a checked cloth, often used for shirts.

clue.text: It may turn mountain road into path

definitions.text: It may turn mountain road into path

parts.words: It may turn mountain road into path
parts.note: a speech defect saying th for s turns pass, a mountain road, into path

explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment where s is sounded as th turns pass into path.

clue.text: Crazy roadways moments

indicators.note: crazy signals that the letters of the next two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Moments of insanity on the highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges ROADWAYS MOMENTS, and the whole clue describes reckless high-speed driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous fast driving in fog on major roads is described as craziness on highways.
